# E004 -- American Express Communication Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Source:** American_Express_Guidelines.pdf
- **Brand:** American Express
- **Industry:** Financial Services
- **Year:** 2018 (June)
- **Pages Sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13
- **Total Pages:** 23
- **Document Type:** Communication Guidelines

## Brand Strategy
- Communication guidelines (not a full brand book) -- focused on how to LOOK
- Product lines referenced: Centurion Line, Standard Blue Box Line, Cobrand communications
- Cardmember-centric brand philosophy: "the Cardmember is the hero, the Card/service is the enabler"
- Tagline is mandatory on promotional/advertising pieces; optional on transactional/informational

## Logo
- **Blue Box logo:** Primary mark, must appear prominently on all communications
- **Alternate logo:** Cropped to "AM EX" -- reserved for small-scale digital use only
- **Logotypes:** Two variants available as alternatives to the logo; logo can still complement logotype at smaller size
- Clear space rules strictly enforced
- Do not place on flat blue backgrounds too close to Blue Box color
- Do not place on competing/busy imagery
- Do not use Blue Box as inline text replacing "American Express"
- Lock-up rules: horizontal pairing with partner logos (with or without dividing line); never vertically stacked
- No new logo treatments or lock-ups may be created externally -- only by American Express

## Typography
- **Sans-serif:** Benton Sans
- **Serif:** Guardian
- Four approved combinations of these two typefaces
- Typography is mandatory when communications include copy

## Color
- Brand color palette: Bright Blue, Deep Blue, and Neutrals palette
- If color is used, only brand colors permitted
- Rich color preferred in photography

## Graphics / Iconography
- Not covered in sampled pages

## Photography
- **Subject matter:** Aspirational but attainable; authentic, real, less stereotypical
- **People:** At least two people interacting, sharing experiences; diversity in gender, ethnicity, age, body types
- **Composition:** Uncluttered backgrounds to maximize ad legibility; moment as focal point (people enjoying, not just scenery)
- **Color:** Rich, saturated color preferred
- **Do not:** Use busy backgrounds, stereotypical images, ostentatious subject matter (e.g. silver service, butlers), artificial filters, posed shots
- Global photo library available through AmEx representatives

## Applications
- Card design referenced (with issuer logo, member since, rewards program placement)
- Partner co-branding lock-up specifications
- Promotional, offering, and advertising pieces

## Tone of Voice
- Not explicitly covered in sampled pages (guide is visual-focused)

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- Concise 23-page guide focused on essential visual identity rules
- Strong photography direction with clear do's/don'ts -- emphasis on diversity and authenticity
- Strict external control: no new logo treatments permitted outside AmEx
- "AM EX" cropped alternate logo for small digital contexts is a notable modern adaptation
- Product line differentiation (Centurion, Standard, Cobrand) affects which rules apply

## Quality Score
4 / 5
- Well-organized, concise communication guide with clear visual rules
- Excellent photography direction with modern diversity/authenticity standards
- Strong logo usage rules with practical do's/don'ts
- Limited scope (23 pages) -- not a full brand identity system; missing detailed color specs, icon system, and tone of voice
